messages.author: 1641d619313d04ab
messages.subject: Step Size and Standard Deviation
parts:
Hi Everyone,

I am running a really simple model, and in the transformed parameters shunk I need to obtain the standard deviation of a vector... then I am typing:

transformed parameters {
   vector[ T ] Index;
   real sdIndex;
   Index <- <...CODE...>;
   sdIndex <- sd( Index );
}

I need to mark that T was defined in the data shunk. Ok, the compilation have not any problem. However all the times that I try to make sample on this model I recieve an error "Error: No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?".

I found in the mailing list of the users and developers threads talking about these issue. Due this I found that it only happen when I add the sd(). I tried constraints to the lower value of the sdIndex and it not worked, and tried to run several times and always the Error happen!

Is there any way to deal with this thing? Maybe my problem seems wierd, actually I must explain deeply: I am trying modeling a threshold over the predictive distribution of the vector Index, thus I need to obtain this threshold as a function of the standard deviation. I think that it is a short introduction about the need to this statistic.

Thank you indeed for any suggestion! I am currently avaliable for any questions and if it is necessary I can share the entirely code!

Cheers,
FH

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Step Size and Standard Deviation
parts:
FH,

Can you provide the whole Stan model? It's hard to tell what's happening with just the transformed parameters block.

Do you have any parameters defined? If you're not using the sdIndex variable in the model, you should move it to the generated quantities block.

Daniel

Hi Daniel,

Before everything I need to say thank you for your care in help.

I read the Stan reference manual about the generated quantities block and how that "parameter" sdI is actually just a forward evaluation I put this things in the correct place and solved the issue.

Thank you indeed. Once more a quick and right answer of the Stan's comunity :)

P.S.: I did a mistake write shunk isntead of chunk or block following the stan notation... I am sorry!

Cheers,
FH
